characters.name: Cedric Daniels
characters.roleStart: Lieutenant running Evidence Control in the basement, a punishment for the Barksdale case; has put in his papers to leave and practise law
characters.roleEnd: Lieutenant commanding the detail, which Burrell has committed to keep together as a major case squad in CID
characters.bio: After the Barksdale case, Daniels is sent to Evidence Control. He puts in his papers and plans to practise law, until Valchek demands him by name to run the detail on Frank Sobotka. He uses that leverage to pick his own people and to get Burrell's promise of a permanent major case unit. He takes on Rawls's fourteen Jane Does in exchange for McNulty and follows the case past Sobotka to the Greek. The Greek escapes and Sobotka is murdered, but the arrests and the cleared murders put Daniels back in the department's favour.

keyMoments.text: Running the evidence room, he has the basement searched for Bunk's missing Gant evidence.
Burrell offers him a major's posting. Daniels asks for more: if he brings in the case, the detail becomes a permanent major case unit in CID, and he picks his own people.
Agrees to take Rawls's Jane Doe murders in return for Rawls's full support, and tells Marla he is 'playing their game' from now on.
The raids find the warehouse stripped. He is furious that Homicide never told the detail Ziggy had killed Glekas.
Talks Valchek out of charging Prez and tells him Burrell has committed to keeping the crew together as a major case squad.

characters.assignmentEnd: Commander of the detail, to continue as a major case squad working out of CID
characters.unofficialNote: The detail is Valchek's creation. Burrell tells Daniels to keep Valchek 'stroked', so Daniels briefs him. Valchek turns on the detail when it moves past Sobotka (ep 9-10).

careerMoves.text: Tells Marla he will put in his papers. He withdraws them when Burrell offers him the detail (ep 3-4).
Burrell gives him the detail Valchek demanded. Rawls signs off on his list of people.

careerMoves.to: Major (posting held by a Major Scalise, due to retire)
careerMoves.text: Burrell offers him a major's posting if he does 'a good turn' on the detail. He is still a lieutenant at the finale.

careerMoves.to: Permanent major case squad in CID
careerMoves.text: Says Burrell is committed to keeping his crew together as a major case squad working out of CID.

characters.name: Stanislaus Valchek
characters.roleStart: Major commanding the Southeastern District
characters.bio: The Southeastern District commander loses a petty feud with stevedore leader Frank Sobotka over who gets the window spot at St. Casimir's church. Wondering how the union can afford it, he trades First District council support for Burrell's commissioner bid in return for a police detail against Sobotka. When the case moves beyond Sobotka, he hands it to the FBI and berates the detail, and his son-in-law Prez punches him. Meanwhile the union has stolen his district surveillance van and keeps mailing him photos of it from ports around the world.

keyMoments.text: Brings a memorial window for Polish police and firefighters to St. Casimir's and finds Sobotka's local already has the spot in the nave.
Has his district ticket the union's cars and run a DWI checkpoint. Trades council support to Burrell for a detail on Sobotka.
Finds his detail playing poker and threatens to make Burrell's confirmation 'uglier than you want it' unless he gets a real detail under Daniels.
Takes the case to the FBI and asks them to recover his van. Then he storms into the detail office, orders Prez out and is punched by him.
Is at the union hall, gloating, when the FBI arrests Sobotka.

characters.unofficialNote: His influence is informal: friends at City Hall and among the First District council members, partly through developer Andy Krawczyk. He uses it as leverage over Burrell ('You owe me on this, Erv').

characters.name: Ervin Burrell
characters.roleStart: Deputy Commissioner for Operations, expected to succeed Commissioner Frazier (who is said to be going to Washington)
characters.roleEnd: Police Commissioner (by ep 9 the council votes are in; many sources call him acting commissioner this season)
characters.bio: With Commissioner Frazier leaving, Burrell is the mayor's choice for the top job but lacks the First District council members. He buys Valchek's help with a six-man detail against Frank Sobotka, staffed with castoffs, and then has to give it to Daniels, the lieutenant he punished, with a promise of a permanent unit. By ep 9 the council votes are in and he is moving into the commissioner's office.

keyMoments.text: Agrees to Valchek's request in exchange for First District support: 'Six men for six weeks. Rawls will pick them.'
Valchek confronts him at a council event over the 'humps' he was sent and demands Daniels.
Offers Daniels a clean slate and a major's posting, and accepts his demands for a permanent unit and his own people.
Tries to calm Valchek when the detail won't charge Sobotka. Valchek accuses him of freezing him out now that 'the votes are in'.
Hears from Daniels, Pearlman, Rawls and the FBI that the case has stalled after Sobotka's murder.

characters.unofficialNote: Politically indebted to Valchek for First District council votes. Daniels' wife Marla reminds Daniels that Burrell 'knows' things about him from 'the bad old days'.

careerMoves.text: Named to succeed Frazier, pending a City Council vote. Valchek calls him 'Deputy' in ep 3; in ep 4 he says the vote is next week.
Valchek: 'the votes are in and you're moving your damn golf trophies upstairs to the commissioner's office'.

characters.name: William Rawls
characters.roleStart: Colonel commanding CID, which includes Homicide (promoted between seasons)
characters.roleEnd: Colonel commanding CID; his fourteen Jane Does are cleared
characters.bio: Now a colonel over CID, Rawls tries to pass off first a harbor floater and then thirteen women dead in a container, but McNulty proves both died within city lines. He gives the fourteen Jane Does to Bunk and Freamon and keeps McNulty on the boat until Daniels agrees to take the murders. At the finale he celebrates when the detail's work clears them.

keyMoments.text: Passes McNulty's floater to Baltimore County. McNulty's tide report sends it back.
Loses the jurisdiction fight with the state police, county and Coast Guard commanders, and fourteen Jane Does go up in red on the Homicide board.
Approves Daniels' list except McNulty: 'He quits or he drowns.'
Lets McNulty join the detail once Daniels has taken the Jane Does.
At the scene where a nine-year-old was killed by a stray bullet, he orders Colvin's district to sweep the drug corners.

careerMoves.text: Promoted between seasons; first seen as a colonel in the premiere.

characters.name: Jay Landsman
characters.roleStart: Sergeant supervising a Homicide squad
characters.bio: Landsman's squad inherits the Jane Does. He gives them to Bunk and Freamon as his 'best people' and is glad to see Daniels' detail take them over. He gets Ziggy Sobotka's signed confession to the Glekas killing but never tells the detail, which gives the Greeks time to clear out their warehouse.

keyMoments.text: Takes the Jane Does from Cole and gives them to Bunk and Freamon.
Welcomes Officer Russell as port police liaison and suggests she wear pantsuits, since Homicide works plainclothes.
Interrogates Ziggy and gets a signed confession.
Daniels berates him for not calling the detail about Glekas.
Celebrates the cleared Jane Does with Rawls.

characters.name: Jimmy McNulty
characters.roleStart: Officer in the Marine Unit, sent there as punishment after the Barksdale case
characters.roleEnd: Officer working on Daniels' detail; pushing to go after Stringer Bell and Proposition Joe next
characters.bio: Stuck in the Marine Unit, McNulty gets back at Rawls by proving that a floater, and then thirteen dead women in a container, belong to the city. He also tries to put a name to the girl he pulled from the harbor. When a reconciliation with Elena fails he goes back to heavy drinking, until Daniels gets him onto the detail. There he goes undercover as a British john at the brothel and photographs the Greek by chance. In the finale he and Kima photograph Stringer Bell meeting Proposition Joe and push Daniels to make them the next case.

keyMoments.text: Uses tide charts to prove the floater went into the water inside city limits, sending the case back to Rawls.
Shows the container's air pipe was crushed deliberately, which makes the deaths homicides.
Sleeps with Elena after a dinner date. In ep 7 she tells him she can never trust him again.
Goes undercover at the brothel and is found having sex with two of the women when the raid team arrives.
With Kima, photographs Stringer meeting Proposition Joe and argues for that case.

characters.rankEnd: Officer (working as an investigator on Daniels' detail)
characters.assignmentEnd: Daniels' detail (to continue as a major case squad)
characters.unofficialNote: Works informal back channels: FBI agent Fitzhugh (ep 9), the medical examiner (ep 2-3), and a federal agent, Cleary (ep 5), to identify his Jane Doe.

careerMoves.text: Daniels asks for him; Rawls refuses: 'He quits or he drowns.'
Rawls gives in after Daniels takes the Jane Doe murders and insists on McNulty.

characters.name: Bunk Moreland
characters.roleStart: Homicide detective preparing the Gant murder trial
characters.roleEnd: Homicide detective; the fourteen Jane Does are cleared
characters.bio: Bunk presses McNulty to find Omar for Bird's trial for the Gant murder, then catches the fourteen Jane Does with Freamon and port officer Beadie Russell. Rawls makes clear he expects them cleared, so Bunk works them out of Daniels' detail office. In the finale he and Beadie find security tape placing Sergei at the Philadelphia killing, and Sergei's admission clears the Jane Does.

keyMoments.text: Asks McNulty to find Omar for the Gant trial.
With Freamon, lets the Atlantic Light sail after its crew pretend not to speak English.
Bird is convicted with Omar's testimony. Bunk tells McNulty that Rawls will force him out if the Jane Does stay open.
With Fitz, traces Vondas's text messages, which are written in Greek.
Philadelphia port security tape breaks Sergei, who says Vondas killed the crewman behind the women's deaths.

characters.assignmentEnd: Homicide (Landsman's squad); worked the Jane Does inside Daniels' detail

careerMoves.text: Landsman reassigns the cases from Cole to Bunk and Freamon.
Tells McNulty that Rawls expects him to clear the cases or will force him out of the unit.

characters.name: Lester Freamon
characters.roleStart: Homicide detective, Bunk's new partner
characters.roleEnd: Detective on Daniels' detail; takes down the case board, leaving the Greek's photo up
characters.bio: Freamon begins the season in Homicide as Bunk's partner on the Jane Does until Rawls temporarily details him to Daniels. He spots Sobotka's link to the dead women, follows the union's political money, and with Beadie uses the cloned port computers to tie missing containers to Horseface and the Greeks' warehouse. At the end he takes down the detail's board but leaves up the photo of the Greek.

keyMoments.text: Gets the Jane Does with Bunk.
Detailed to the Sobotka detail, he recognises Frank Sobotka from his photo and links him to the Jane Does.
Finds $70,000 in union political contributions and ties the missing containers to Horseface.
The decoy container gives the detail Vondas's phone number.
Takes Nick Sobotka to the detail when he surrenders at the Southeastern desk.

characters.assignmentEnd: Daniels' detail (to continue as a major case squad)

careerMoves.text: Rawls: 'You need to get over to the Southeastern today. You're detailed temporarily.'

characters.name: Kima Greggs
characters.roleStart: Detective at a desk job in the Asset Forfeiture unit, in her second year of pre-law
characters.roleEnd: Detective on Daniels' detail, pushing to go after Stringer Bell and Proposition Joe
characters.bio: Recovered from her shooting, Kima has kept her promise to Cheryl: a desk job in Asset Forfeiture and pre-law classes. Daniels draws her back to street work on the detail. She works the vice angle with Prez and McNulty and leads Herc and Carver's team. At home Cheryl becomes pregnant by artificial insemination, and Kima struggles to share her excitement.

keyMoments.text: Turns down Herc's invitation to join his raids: 'I am inside now.'
Daniels persuades her to join the detail, against Cheryl's wishes.
Through Shardene, finds a dancer who describes the trafficked Eastern European women.
Asks Beadie how she balances police work with being a mother.
Bubbles' tip leads her and McNulty to photograph Stringer meeting Proposition Joe.

characters.assignmentEnd: Daniels' detail (to continue as a major case squad)

careerMoves.text: Daniels recruits her. Cheryl and Marla are both unhappy about it.

characters.name: Herc Hauk
characters.roleStart: Narcotics detective making buys from white dealers (his 'Kane Street case')
characters.roleEnd: Detective on the detail, fed up with surveillance duty; says he will go back to straight narcotics when it ends
characters.bio: Back in Narcotics, Herc is buying drugs from white dealers when Daniels brings him onto the detail. Paired again with Carver, he works the drug trade near the port. When the borrowed bug they hid in a tennis ball is crushed, they invent an informant, 'Fuzzy Dunlop' (Herc's cousin Bernard), to pay for it. Tired of surveillance and errands, he says he will go back to straight narcotics once the detail ends.

keyMoments.text: Mocks Kima for taking a desk job.
The borrowed bug is crushed in traffic after Frog throws the tennis ball.
Registers his cousin as the fake informant 'Fuzzy Dunlop', then does house chores for the duty judge.
He and Carver tell Daniels they are being used as 'pack mules'.

careerMoves.text: Picked by Daniels and approved by Rawls.
Says that when the detail is over he will go back to straight narcotics and find a new 'rabbi'. Not carried out by the finale.

characters.name: Ellis Carver
characters.roleStart: Uniformed sergeant in the Southeastern District under Valchek
characters.roleEnd: Sergeant on the detail; announces he will apply for a sergeant's post in Major Colvin's Western District flex squad
characters.bio: Newly promoted, Carver is a uniformed sergeant in Valchek's Southeastern District, ticketing the stevedores' cars on orders passed down from Valchek. Daniels takes him onto the detail on the theory that a man caught betraying him once won't do it twice. But Daniels says his stripes weren't earned and has him report to Kima. Fed up with being a 'pack mule', Carver tells Daniels in the finale that he will go for a sergeant's opening in Major Colvin's Western District flex squad.

keyMoments.text: Tells Frank the ticketing comes from Valchek, then runs a DWI checkpoint on the stevedores.
Joins the detail. Daniels: 'Your paycheck may say sergeant, but on this detail Det. Greggs runs your team.'
Leaves his credit card as collateral for the bug that gets crushed.
Tells Daniels he will apply for the Western District flex squad post: 'Last time I checked, I had stripes.'

characters.assignmentEnd: Daniels' detail (seeking a transfer to the Western District)

careerMoves.to: Sobotka detail, working as a detective under Greggs
careerMoves.text: Valchek gives Daniels his pick of the district. Daniels won't recognise Carver's rank on the detail.

careerMoves.to: Sergeant, Western District flex squad (DEU) under Major Colvin
careerMoves.text: Says he will apply for the posting he saw. Not yet carried out at the finale.

characters.name: Prez Pryzbylewski
characters.roleStart: Narcotics detective after the Barksdale case; Valchek's son-in-law
characters.roleEnd: Disciplined for punching Valchek: two months on the Southeastern desk on the midnight shift and a letter of apology, after which he may return to Daniels' unit
characters.bio: Prez tells his father-in-law Valchek he wants to work cases, not chase rank, and is put on Valchek's first detail, where Lieutenant Grayson ignores his advice. His complaints to Valchek lead to Daniels taking over. He works the money trail and the vice angle. When Valchek storms in and calls him a 'shitbird', Prez punches him, then hands Daniels his gun. Daniels gets the charges dropped in exchange for two months of midnight desk duty and a letter of apology.

keyMoments.text: Turns down Valchek's plan for him to make sergeant and then lieutenant: 'I don't want to make rank. I want to work cases.'
Tells Valchek the detail is going nowhere under Grayson and that Burrell's interference hurt the Barksdale case.
Traces the union's political contributions with Freamon, then visits strip clubs with Kima on the vice angle.
Punches Valchek in the detail office and hands Daniels his gun.
Off screen, Daniels gets Valchek to drop charges: midnight desk duty for two months and a letter of apology.

characters.assignmentEnd: Southeastern District desk, midnight shift for two months, then free to return to Daniels' unit
characters.unofficialNote: Tells his father-in-law how the first detail is (not) working (ep 3), which Valchek uses to force Burrell to bring in Daniels. Valchek calls him his 'lead investigator' and in ep 10 treats him as his man: 'you ain't gonna use my people to fuck me'.

careerMoves.text: Valchek offers to get him through the sergeant's exam to a quiet day shift in the Southeast. Prez turns it down.
Valchek tells the new detail his son-in-law is the lead investigator.
Valchek orders him off the detail and threatens an insubordination charge. Prez refuses, then punches him.

careerMoves.to: Southeastern District desk, midnight shift (two months)
careerMoves.text: Agreed between Daniels and Valchek in place of assault charges, along with a letter of apology. Prez does not appear in eps 11-12.

characters.name: Beadie Russell
characters.roleStart: Port police officer patrolling the Patapsco terminals, two years on the job
characters.roleEnd: Back at work with the port police after the case
characters.bio: Two years into port police work, after a job taking tolls at the Fort McHenry tunnel, Beadie finds thirteen dead women in a shipping container and is detailed to Homicide as liaison. She learns fast alongside Bunk and Freamon, shows the detail how to track containers on the port computers, makes her first foot pursuit tailing Vondas, and persuades Frank Sobotka, whom she knows from the docks, to cooperate. She is a single mother of two; she flirts with McNulty, but he leaves her house before anything happens. At the end she returns to the port.

keyMoments.text: Notices a broken customs seal and finds the dead women in the container.
Detailed to Homicide as liaison with the port police, the only help her department sends.
Shows Bunk and Daniels how to track container movements on the port database.
Has port officers stop Frank's decoy truck. Frank then learns from port officers that she is detailed to city police, not at the Fairfield piers as she told him.
Tails Vondas on foot to a hotel room, then persuades Frank to cooperate.

characters.unofficialNote: Her port police superiors are never named on screen. During the case she answers to Landsman (ep 3) and then to Daniels' detail (from ep 6).

careerMoves.to: Detailed to BPD Homicide as port police liaison
careerMoves.text: Landsman: 'I am informed that you are detailed to this case as a liaison with the port police.'
Daniels: Russell and Bunk are assigned to Homicide but will run the port database with the detail.
Shown back at work at the port in the closing montage.

characters.name: Claude Diggins
characters.roleStart: Marine Unit officer, McNulty's boat partner
characters.bio: A Marine Unit veteran, Diggins partners McNulty on the boat, complains about his bad knots and covers for his absences. He takes Bunk and McNulty out posing as fishermen to watch Vondas, and in the finale pulls Frank Sobotka's body from the harbor.

keyMoments.text: Takes Bunk and McNulty out on a 'fishing trip' to watch Vondas and Eton drop their phones in the water.
Pulls Frank Sobotka's body from the water in front of the stevedores.

characters.unofficialNote: The Marine Unit has a sergeant ('I gotta tell my Sergeant', ep 1) who is never named.

characters.name: Ray Cole
characters.roleStart: Homicide detective
characters.bio: Cole catches McNulty's harbor floater and briefly holds the Jane Does before Landsman gives them to Bunk and Freamon. He helps serve grand jury summonses on the checkers, and with Norris tries to bluff Bodie over the guns from a child's shooting.

keyMoments.text: Gleefully hands his Jane Doe paperwork to Bunk and Freamon.
Claims Bodie's prints are on the murder gun, picks the wrong gun, and Bodie asks for a lawyer.

characters.name: Ed Norris
characters.roleStart: Homicide detective
characters.bio: Norris is the lead detective on the killing of a nine-year-old by a stray bullet in a West Baltimore turf fight. With Cole he questions Bodie after the dumped guns are recovered from a passing barge.

characters.name: Vernon Holley
characters.roleStart: Homicide detective
characters.bio: In an uncredited appearance, Holley is seen briefly working the scene after Frank Sobotka's body is recovered.

characters.name: Augustus Polk
characters.roleStart: Detective sent to Valchek's first Sobotka detail
characters.roleEnd: Off the detail once Daniels remakes it
characters.bio: Polk is one of the 'humps' sent to Valchek's first detail under Lieutenant Grayson. At the briefing his only concern is who signs off on overtime, and Valchek later finds him playing poker in the office. Daniels' remade detail does not include him.

keyMoments.text: Playing poker in the detail office ('See it or fold, Augie') when Valchek walks in.

characters.assignmentStart: Valchek's detail (unit before that not stated in S2)

careerMoves.text: One of the six men Rawls picks to fill Burrell's promise to Valchek.

characters.name: Grayson
characters.roleStart: Lieutenant commanding the first detail formed for Valchek
characters.roleEnd: Replaced as detail commander by Daniels
characters.bio: Recommended by Burrell as 'really good at property crimes', Lieutenant Grayson commands Valchek's first detail. He doesn't follow Prez's advice: no phone records, no look at union assets. When Valchek visits, Grayson is out and the men are playing poker, so Valchek demands Daniels.
characters.unofficialNote: Mostly discussed rather than seen. Fandom credits an uncredited appearance in ep 3; the actor is unknown.

careerMoves.text: Replaced when Burrell gives the detail to Daniels at Valchek's demand.

characters.name: Michael Santangelo
characters.roleStart: Patrol officer (demoted from Homicide at the end of S1)
characters.bio: Now in uniform, Santangelo arrests Bubbles and Johnny for stealing medical supplies from an ambulance. He lets Kima and McNulty work Bubbles for information ('I owe you one, Sanny').
characters.assignmentStart: Patrol (Western District per the end of S1; the district is not restated in S2)

characters.name: Howard Colvin
characters.roleStart: Major commanding the Western District
characters.bio: The Western District commander arrives late to the scene where a nine-year-old was killed by a stray bullet; he had been in Washington with Burrell, chasing grant money at the Justice Department. Rawls orders him to sweep the corners. He does it, but wonders aloud what they are really doing, chasing the drug trade 'from one corner to the next like it's a plan'.

characters.name: Dennis Mello
characters.roleStart: Lieutenant in the Western District, Colvin's second in command
characters.bio: In an uncredited appearance, Colvin's lieutenant is at the scene of the child's shooting and remarks that the sweep of the drug corners came too late.
characters.unofficialNote: Name and rank come from the credits and the fan wiki; neither is spoken in ep 9.

characters.name: Terrance Fitzhugh
characters.roleStart: FBI special agent, Baltimore field office
characters.roleEnd: FBI special agent on the joint case; has worked out where the leak came from
characters.bio: McNulty's FBI contact looks up Glekas for him and finds the file sealed by an Agent Koutris. When Valchek brings in the Bureau, Fitz works the case with the detail: he traces Vondas's texts and helps arrest Sergei. At the end he learns Koutris left the San Diego office more than a year ago for counterterrorism in Washington. He tells Daniels, off the record, that the leak came from the Bureau's side.

keyMoments.text: Finds Glekas's FBI file sealed by Agent Koutris.
Arrives at the detail with the FBI team and helps trace Vondas's text messages.
Arrests Sergei at his home with McNulty.
Learns Koutris is in counterterrorism in Washington and tells Daniels the leak wasn't from his people.

characters.assignmentEnd: FBI Baltimore field office; joint case with the detail
characters.unofficialNote: A back channel for McNulty and Daniels. He tells Daniels about the leak with 'I never told you this'.

characters.name: Amanda Reese
characters.roleStart: FBI supervisor
characters.roleEnd: FBI supervisor; pressing the union to replace its leadership or be decertified
characters.bio: Fitz's supervisor accepts the case Valchek brings and shares it with Daniels and Pearlman as a RICO case. Since 9/11 the Bureau's one priority here is waterfront corruption, so its focus is the union. At the arrest she holds Sobotka inside until the press arrives. After Sobotka's death the Bureau tells the stevedores to elect new officers or have the local decertified.

keyMoments.text: Agrees to a joint RICO case focused on the union.
Delays taking Sobotka out of the union hall until the press arrive.

characters.name: Kristos Koutris
characters.roleStart: FBI agent with the counterterrorism people in Washington, secretly passing information to the Greek
characters.roleEnd: Same; Fitz suspects him, but nothing is done by the finale
characters.bio: An FBI agent in counterterrorism in Washington, Koutris feeds the Greek information about investigations. He warns that agents are asking about Glekas, explains how the FBI is tracking the Greeks, and finally reports that Frank Sobotka has agreed to cooperate, just as Frank goes to meet the Greek. The Greek in turn gives him a large Colombian cocaine shipment, which Koutris seizes.

keyMoments.text: Seals Glekas's file and tips the Greeks off when Fitz asks about him. The Greek gives him a Colombian cocaine shipment to seize.
Meets the Greek and tells him the Bureau is on the port unions with wiretaps.
Tells the Greek that Sobotka has met with the police and agreed to inform.

characters.assignmentStart: FBI counterterrorism, Washington (Fitz believed he was in the San Diego field office)
characters.unofficialNote: Leaks FBI case information to the Greek. Fitz implies the counterterrorism side values the Greek as a source after 9/11.

characters.name: Salmond
characters.roleStart: FBI special agent
characters.bio: One of Reese's agents on the joint case, who offers to help trace the origin of the stolen containers.
characters.unofficialNote: Uncredited in eps 10-11 per fan wiki.

characters.name: Mason
characters.roleStart: FBI special agent
characters.bio: Arrives at the detail with Agent Settles ('Maj. Valchek said you'd be expecting us') when the FBI joins the case.
characters.unofficialNote: Fan wiki credits William L. Thomas as 'FBI Special Agent Mason' in ep 10 and as an unnamed 'FBI Agent' in eps 11-12.

characters.name: Settles
characters.roleStart: FBI special agent
characters.bio: Mason's partner, named when the two agents introduce themselves at the detail office.
characters.unofficialNote: Actor unverified; possibly Kevin McKelvy, credited only as 'FBI Agent'.

characters.name: Cleary
characters.unit: Federal agent handling human trafficking and deportations (FBI per fan wiki; INS per Wikipedia)
characters.roleStart: Federal special agent
characters.bio: A federal agent who briefs the Jane Doe investigators on the international sex trade. Later he lets McNulty look through records of undocumented women from his field office and interview some being held in New Jersey, though he can't see why McNulty cares about identifying the girl.
characters.assignmentStart: Federal field office covering Maryland and Delaware

characters.name: Marcus Lemmell
characters.unit: Federal agent handling human trafficking (FBI per fan wiki)
characters.roleStart: Federal special agent, partnered with Cleary
characters.bio: With Cleary, he tells Bunk, Freamon and Beadie that the French addresses on the container paperwork are false and explains how much money the trafficked women are worth.

characters.name: Robert Norris
characters.unit: Maryland State Police (the state side of the port jurisdiction)
characters.roleStart: Colonel, Maryland State Police
characters.bio: The colonel Rawls calls 'Robbie' concedes that the container deaths are technically the port police's, but argues that the port police aren't equipped for a death investigation and that his state police would have to pick up the slack. Rawls refuses to 'eat' thirteen murders, and the meeting with the county and Coast Guard commanders ends with the Jane Does in the city.
characters.unofficialNote: Only 'Robbie' and 'colonel' are spoken. The surname and the title 'Superintendent, Maryland State Police' come from the fan wiki. Wikipedia calls this commander 'Ronnie, the commander of the Port Authority', which looks wrong. The faction is set to mdta only because the list has no state police option.

characters.name: Rhonda Pearlman
characters.roleStart: Assistant State's Attorney
characters.roleEnd: Assistant State's Attorney; prosecuting Eton and Horseface
characters.bio: Pearlman ends her casual affair with McNulty early in the season, then returns as the detail's courthouse liaison. She gets its wiretaps signed and witnesses McNulty's statement after the brothel raid. She shares the case with the FBI and federal prosecutors, offers Frank and Nick straight probation for Frank's cooperation, and is shown prosecuting Eton and Horseface at the end.

keyMoments.text: Tells McNulty not to come to her house again.
Takes the detail's wiretap affidavits to the duty judge, Vanderwal.
Agrees to straight probation for Frank and Nick if Frank cooperates fully.
Prosecutes Eton and Horseface in the closing montage.

characters.assignmentEnd: Baltimore City State's Attorney's Office; legal liaison to the detail

characters.name: Ilene Nathan
characters.roleStart: Assistant State's Attorney prosecuting Bird for the Gant murder
characters.roleEnd: Assistant State's Attorney; won the conviction
characters.bio: Nathan prosecutes Bird for the Gant murder and pushes Bunk and McNulty to produce Omar or she drops the charges. She thinks Omar a sociopath but is thrilled when his testimony holds up against Levy, and afterward gives him a pass on a future minor charge.

keyMoments.text: Interviews Omar and gives McNulty a voucher to buy him court clothes.
Wins Bird's conviction on Omar's testimony.

characters.unofficialNote: Ep 4 appearance is voice only per fan wiki.

characters.name: Daniel Phelan
characters.roleStart: Circuit Court judge
characters.bio: Phelan presides over Bird's trial, is entertained by Omar's testimony, denies an appeal bond and signals that Bird will get life.

characters.name: Vanderwal
characters.roleStart: Judge on wiretap duty that week
characters.bio: The week's duty judge signs the detail's wiretap orders, then has Herc and Carver move an air conditioner and wash his windows.
characters.unofficialNote: Named in dialogue ('Who's the duty judge this week? Vanderwal.'). The actor is not credited.

characters.name: Gary DiPasquale
characters.roleStart: Grand jury prosecutor
characters.bio: Runs the grand jury before which Bunk summons the checkers who worked the Atlantic Light. He tells Bunk the hearings produced little.
characters.unofficialNote: Uncredited; the name comes from the fan wiki and is not spoken on screen.

characters.name: Nadiva Bryant
characters.roleStart: Assistant U.S. Attorney
characters.bio: The federal prosecutor on the joint FBI case, which is set up as a RICO prosecution in federal court.

characters.name: Maurice Levy
characters.roleStart: Defense attorney for the Barksdale organization
characters.roleEnd: Defense attorney for the Barksdale organization
characters.bio: Levy negotiates Avon's deal: information on the prison overdose deaths in exchange for an earlier parole hearing, which leads to guard Tilghman's arrest. He loses Bird's trial after Omar turns his cross-examination back on him ('I got the shotgun, you got the briefcase').

characters.name: Clay Davis
characters.roleStart: State senator from the west side
characters.roleEnd: State senator; breaks ground on the condominiums replacing the grain pier
characters.bio: At a political evening at the church, the union's lobbyist steers Frank toward Senator Davis, whose Westside organization has taken $40,000 from the union and still has its hand out. After the arrests the union's political support collapses, and Davis is at the groundbreaking for condominiums where the grain pier was to be revived.

keyMoments.text: Frank has to court him despite the $40,000 already given.
Breaks ground on the grain pier condominiums.

characters.unofficialNote: Also researched in union.json.

characters.name: Andy Krawczyk
characters.roleStart: Property developer and political fundraiser with City Hall's ear; Valchek's friend
characters.roleEnd: Developer of the grain pier condominiums
characters.bio: Valchek boasts that he has Krawczyk's ear and that Krawczyk has City Hall's. Krawczyk tells him Sobotka's struggling union is spending heavily on contributions and a lobbyist, which feeds Valchek's suspicion. He is at the condominium groundbreaking at the end.

keyMoments.text: Tells Valchek the union is 'throwing around a lot of cash' on politics.

characters.unofficialNote: Also researched in union.json. Uncredited in ep 12 per fan wiki.

characters.name: Marla Daniels
characters.roleStart: Daniels' wife, urging him to leave the department and practise law
characters.roleEnd: Daniels' wife, estranged over his choice to stay
characters.bio: Marla urges Daniels to resign and use his law degree, then storms out of dinner when he takes the detail. She warns him Burrell won't forget what he knows about him, and tells him what she first loved in him was his ambition.

characters.name: Elena McNulty
characters.roleStart: McNulty's estranged wife, a realtor
characters.roleEnd: McNulty's estranged wife; won't trust him again
characters.bio: Elena, now a realtor, sends McNulty a separation agreement and shows a house to Nick Sobotka and Aimee. She sleeps with McNulty after a dinner date, then asks him to leave before the boys see him and tells him she can never trust him again.

characters.name: Cheryl
characters.roleStart: Kima's partner, planning a child by artificial insemination
characters.bio: Cheryl wants Kima safe at a desk and starting a family. She resents Kima's return to detective work and insists on coming along to the strip club. She becomes pregnant and is frustrated by Kima's lack of enthusiasm.

characters.name: Shardene Innes
characters.roleStart: Former dancer, in nursing school with Freamon's encouragement
characters.bio: Now in nursing school ('Lester's been pushing me'), Shardene connects Kima with a dancer friend who describes the trafficked Eastern European women and the madam who controls them.

characters.name: Sean McNulty
characters.roleStart: McNulty's elder son, living with Elena
characters.bio: In uncredited appearances, McNulty brings his sons home to Elena after an evening out.

characters.name: Michael McNulty
characters.roleStart: McNulty's younger son, living with Elena
characters.bio: In uncredited appearances, McNulty brings his sons home to Elena after an evening out.

characters.name: Randall Frazier
characters.roleStart: Medical examiner
characters.bio: The medical examiner first calls the container deaths probably accidental. After McNulty points out the pounding marks on the air pipe, he tells him he has 'bought yourself 13 homicides', helps time the deaths, and traces breast implants on three of the women to Budapest.
characters.assignmentStart: Office of the Chief Medical Examiner
characters.assignmentEnd: Office of the Chief Medical Examiner

Head of the department, appointed by the mayor and confirmed by City Council. Frazier is leaving at the start; Burrell is commissioner-designate (often called acting commissioner) until the council vote, which has happened by ep 9.

ladder.acting: Burrell is commissioner-designate, widely described as acting commissioner, from ep 2 until the council vote. By ep 9 Valchek says the votes are in. Daniels' squad is a temporary detail until ep 12, when Burrell commits to making it a permanent major case squad in CID; Daniels stays a lieutenant.
ladder.portPolice: Beadie belongs to the port police, which BPD characters call the Port Authority or port police. In ep 4 she says she got the job from an MDOT posting for 'Port Authority officers, Schedule one, starting at $33,000', after taking tolls at the Fort McHenry tunnel. Wikipedia calls her an MDTA officer and the fan wiki a Maryland Port Administration officer. It is a state agency outside the BPD chain, with jurisdiction over Port Authority property such as the Patapsco terminals. In ep 2 a state police colonel argues the port police 'are not equipped for a death investigation', so the state police would have to take it. Her rank is Officer. Her own superiors are never named, and in ep 3 Landsman notes she is 'the only help that your department is sending'. She is detailed to BPD Homicide as liaison (ep 3), works from Daniels' detail office from ep 6, and returns to the port at the finale.

orgStructure.notes: Burrell moves from Deputy Commissioner (Operations) to commissioner, with the council votes in by ep 9. Frazier is leaving and never seen. The mayor (unnamed) picks the commissioner and the City Council confirms. Burrell took district commanders to the Justice Department in Washington for grant money (ep 9).
Rawls is a colonel over CID: 'the detail is investigative and comes under CID' (ep 4). The link to Burrell is inferred; no deputy commissioner sits between them on screen.

Landsman's squad works directly for Rawls on screen; no Homicide lieutenant, captain or major is shown. Freamon is detailed to Daniels in ep 5. Bunk works the Jane Does from the detail office from ep 6-7.
Daniels' punishment posting in the basement, eps 1-3.

At the start Herc works narcotics cases and Kima has a desk in the Asset Forfeiture unit ('I write all the affidavits and the filing for the City Solicitor'). Prez wants to stay in Narcotics. No commander is shown.

Carver ('word comes down this morning from my shift lieutenant') tickets the union's cars on Valchek's orders. The district has a DEU, and the detail's offices and Nick's warrant are at the Southeastern. Valchek's district surveillance van is stolen by the union (ep 2).
Seen in ep 9 at the scene of the child's shooting; Rawls orders the sweep. Carver eyes a Western District flex squad sergeant's post under Colvin (ep 12). Santangelo's district is not restated in S2.
Led by an unnamed sergeant. McNulty is there as punishment until ep 8.
'Six men for six weeks. Rawls will pick them' (ep 2). Valchek calls it 'my detail' and Prez his lead investigator. The other members are unnamed. It is replaced by Daniels' detail in ep 4.

Formally under CID with Rawls approving staff. Politically it is Valchek's creation, and Burrell promised Daniels a permanent unit. Pearlman is the legal liaison. Kima runs the Herc/Carver street team. Beadie and Bunk are formally Homicide (and port police) but work from the detail's office. The FBI joins in ep 10.

unitFormation.name: The detail (fan wiki: 'Sobotka detail')
unitFormation.why: A grudge. In ep 1 Valchek arrives at St. Casimir's church with a $2,500 memorial window for Polish police and firefighters, and finds Frank Sobotka's stevedore local has already paid more for the spot in the nave with a window from Esslingen, Germany. Father Lewandowski offers him the rectory hallway instead. Valchek asks how a union with fewer than 100 dues-payers can afford it, confronts Frank (ep 2) and has his district paper the union's cars and stop them at a DWI checkpoint. The union retaliates by stealing his district surveillance van and shipping it around the world. Developer Andy Krawczyk tells him the union is spending heavily on a lobbyist and contributions, and Valchek decides Sobotka is 'into some dirt'.
unitFormation.arrangedBy: Valchek and Burrell (ep 2). Burrell needs the First District council members, who are 'pushing Shipley', for his confirmation as commissioner. Valchek offers to bring them in and asks for a detail of 'CID people mostly'. Burrell: 'Six men for six weeks. Rawls will pick them.'
unitFormation.firstVersion: Eps 2-3. Lt. Grayson, recommended by Burrell as 'good at property crimes', leads Prez (Valchek's 'lead investigator'), Polk and other castoffs from port-side offices. They run no DNRs and look at no union assets. In ep 3 Valchek finds them playing poker with the lieutenant out. He hears from Prez that Burrell hobbled the Barksdale case, and threatens at a council event to make Burrell's confirmation 'uglier than you want it' unless he gets 'a real detail, with real police and a real unit commander' under 'that black lieutenant that did Barksdale'.
unitFormation.daniels_terms: In ep 4 Burrell offers Daniels, who has filed his papers, a clean slate and the major's posting a Major Scalise will vacate. Daniels sees that Valchek asked for him by name and demands two things: if he brings in the case, the detail becomes permanent 'as a major case unit within CID', and he chooses his own people. Burrell: 'Make a list. Give it to Rawls.'

unitFormation.jane_doe_merger: In ep 7 Rawls asks Daniels to take the fourteen Jane Does and Daniels refuses ('That case is a loser'). Freamon, Bunk and Beadie persuade him, and he takes them on condition that Rawls gives him everything he asks for. He uses that in ep 8 to get McNulty.
unitFormation.fbi_merger: In ep 10, angry that the case has moved past Sobotka, Valchek gives the detail's material to the FBI and asks them to quietly find his van. Reese's squad and AUSA Bryant agree to share a RICO case with Daniels and Pearlman, on condition that the focus stays on the union ('As of 9/11, the Bureau has one priority in this case: it's waterfront corruption'). Logging the case into FBI systems alerts Agent Koutris, who tips off the Greek. In ep 11 Koutris tells the Greek that Sobotka has agreed to cooperate.

unitBreakup.summary: The case 'hits the wall' in ep 12. Frank Sobotka is murdered before giving a formal statement. Nick and Sergei cooperate, but Vondas and the Greek leave the country hours ahead of the detail. The Jane Does are cleared on Sergei's account, and Eton, Sergei, White Mike, the madam and Horseface are charged. The FBI uses the case to force the union to change leadership or face decertification, and U.S. Marshals close the union hall. Daniels tells Valchek that Burrell is committed to keeping the crew together as a major case squad in CID. Over drinks, Kima and McNulty pitch Proposition Joe and Stringer Bell as its next target.

uncertainties: Burrell's title: Valchek calls him 'Deputy' in ep 3, he says the council vote is 'next week' in ep 4, and in ep 9 Valchek says 'the votes are in' and he is moving to the commissioner's office. Wikipedia and the fan wiki call him Acting Commissioner throughout S2. rankEnd is set to Commissioner.
Frazier's exit: the only line is 'If the commissioner goes down to Washington, it's you' (ep 2). Wikipedia and the fan wiki call it a retirement.
Port police naming: the dialogue says 'Port Authority', 'port police' and an MDOT job posting. Wikipedia says MDTA officer; the fan wiki says Maryland Port Administration officer.

The ep 2 jurisdiction meeting: Rawls calls the other colonel 'Robbie', and his lines ('MSP is gonna have to pick up that slack') mark him as state police. The fan wiki names him Robert Norris, MSP superintendent; Wikipedia calls him 'Ronnie, the commander of the Port Authority', apparently mixing him up with McNulty's 'Ronnie' (Rhonda Pearlman). Actor unknown. The faction is set to mdta for lack of a state police option.
Beadie's port police superiors and McNulty's Marine Unit sergeant are never named.
Lt. Grayson: first name and actor unknown; he may be seen only uncredited in ep 3.
Judge Vanderwal: named in dialogue (ep 8), actor not credited.
Cleary and Lemmell: the fan wiki says FBI, Wikipedia calls Cleary INS. The dialogue (undocumented women, deportations, a Maryland/Delaware field office) fits either.

Koutris: the first name 'Kristos' comes from credits and wikis, not dialogue. Ep 9 places him in FBI counterterrorism in Washington. In ep 12 Fitz learns he left the San Diego field office more than a year earlier for counterterrorism at headquarters.
Agent Settles: actor unverified (possibly Kevin McKelvy, credited as 'FBI Agent'). Mason's actor comes from the fan wiki's ep 10 cast list.
No Homicide lieutenant, captain or major appears; Landsman deals directly with Rawls. Reporting lines from Rawls, Valchek and Colvin up to Burrell are inferred.
Polk's unit before and after the first detail is not stated in S2. The fan wiki says Property Crimes.
Daniels' major's posting (a Major Scalise retiring 'this summer') is offered in ep 4. He is still a lieutenant at the finale; the permanent unit was promised and Burrell is said to be committed.
Carver's Western District move and Herc's return to narcotics are only intentions at the finale.
Prez's sanction is stated by Valchek in ep 12. Prez is credited but not seen in eps 11-12.
Shardene living with Freamon (fan wiki) is not explicit in S2. On screen she is in nursing school and says 'Lester's been pushing me'.
Wikipedia says Daniels and Marla begin sleeping in separate rooms. Not verified in the transcripts, so left out.
Wikipedia says Valchek whispers 'rest in peace' in Polish after Sobotka's death. Not verified, so left out.

Who held Sobotka for the press: Wikipedia's ep 11 article says Reese; Wikipedia's Valchek article says Valchek arrested him personally. The fan wiki has Valchek and Reese waiting together with Valchek gloating. Reese delaying for the press and Valchek gloating are used here.
Valchek's wife: the anniversary toast in ep 3 is 'To Stan and Kate'. Prez's wife is not identified on screen; the fan wiki calls her Joan. She is not included as a character.
Holley's ep 12 appearance, Cole's episodes, Mello's name and DiPasquale's name come from fan wiki cast lists. Mello and DiPasquale are not named in dialogue.
McNulty's rank: he is addressed as 'Officer McNulty' (eps 3 and 5). Nothing on screen says he regains detective status when he joins the detail.
Not included: MSP detective Kevin Reynolds (prison overdose probe, Barksdale storyline, uncredited), Tactical/QRT leader 'Torret' and Western officer Eddie Walker (uncredited, ep 9).
Bruce DiBiago and Father Lewandowski are covered in union.json and only referenced here.
